Australia Tightens Student Visa Rules: What Indian Students and Parents Must Do Now

30 Oct 2026, 06:37 AM IST · GlobeWire Daily World Desk · Source: www.indiatoday.in

Key takeaways New Biometric Checks and Transfer Limits Take Effect Starting October 26, 2026, Indian students applying for Australian student visas will be required to submit fingerprints and a facial image as part of expanded biometric checks. The change applies only to fresh appl

New Biometric Checks and Transfer Limits Take Effect

Starting October 26, 2026, Indian students applying for Australian student visas will be required to submit fingerprints and a facial image as part of expanded biometric checks. The change applies only to fresh applications; those submitted before the date remain unaffected. The Australian Department of Home Affairs has not released a detailed FAQ, but immigration experts advise monitoring official communications for precise instructions.

Longer Restriction on Changing Universities

Effective October 2, 2026, most international students face a 12‑month waiting period before they can switch education providers, up from the previous six‑month limit. Exceptions exist for specific circumstances, but the default rule means students must research courses and institutions carefully before enrolling. The longer restriction raises the stakes for initial course selection and can impact academic planning.

Financial Planning and Employment Realities

Ankit Aggarwal, CEO of Unstop, stresses that families should evaluate the full cost of study, including tuition, rent, food, insurance, and currency fluctuations. He also cautions against assuming an Australian degree guarantees employment or permanent residency. Unstop’s Talent Report 2026 shows that 85 % of engineering graduates, 84 % of undergraduates, and 74 % of B‑school graduates remained unplaced at the time of the survey, underscoring the need for realistic career preparation.

Five Practical Steps for Students and Parents

1. Understand Visa Requirements

  • Monitor official updates from Australia’s Department of Home Affairs.
  • Prepare accurate academic transcripts, financial evidence, and any required biometric data.
  • Avoid agents promising guaranteed visa outcomes.

2. Research Courses and Institutions

  • Compare tuition fees, course content, location, support services, and post‑graduation pathways.
  • Review enrolment conditions and the rules governing provider changes.

3. Prepare a Realistic Budget

  • Include tuition, accommodation, meals, transport, health insurance, utilities, and emergency funds.
  • Do not rely on part‑time work to cover essential expenses or compromise on safe housing.

4. Prioritise Accommodation Safety

  • Verify property listings and providers; assess neighbourhood safety and transport links.
  • Review rental agreements carefully and keep payment receipts.
  • When arranging housing remotely, avoid transferring money based solely on unverified listings or pressure from unknown intermediaries.

5. Prepare for Independent Living

  • Familiarise yourself with local emergency services, campus support, transport options, and student welfare resources.
  • Discuss personal safety, financial responsibility, and emergency plans with parents before departure.

Saurabh Arora, CEO of University Living, notes that while affordable accommodation is important, it should never come at the cost of a student’s safety and well‑being.

What’s Confirmed and What Remains Unknown

Confirmed

  • Biometric collection (fingerprints and facial image) for new visa applications from 26 Oct 2026.
  • 12‑month restriction on changing education providers, effective 2 Oct 2026.
  • Expert‑provided checklists and financial impact warnings.

Uncertain

  • Exact list of exceptions to the transfer restriction.
  • Future adjustments to biometric procedures or additional documentation requirements.
  • Detailed cost breakdowns for living expenses in specific Australian cities.

How Readers Can Verify the Information

The original announcement and detailed guidance are published on India Today’s website: https://www.indiatoday.in/education-today/study-abroad/story/australia-student-visa-rules-transfer-limits-biometric-checks-indian-students-parents-checklist-study-abroad-3025929-2026-10-27. Readers should consult the official Australian Department of Home Affairs immigration portal for the most current visa guidelines and any supplementary updates.

Practical Implications for Indian Families

The tightened rules mean that Indian families must shift from a reactive to a proactive approach. Early and thorough research can prevent costly mid‑course transfers, while comprehensive budgeting protects against unexpected financial strain. The biometric requirement adds a procedural step but does not alter eligibility criteria; however, it does increase the administrative load for applicants. Overall, the changes aim to ensure that students commit to reputable institutions and are financially prepared, reducing the risk of overstayers and undocumented work.

By following the five‑step checklist and staying informed through official channels, Indian students and their parents can navigate the new requirements with confidence and focus on achieving their academic and career goals in Australia.
